title: Unclear, then clear after two questions: 'the car is doing that thing again'
demonstrates: Rule R13 on a drafts channel. The clarifying question is the draft; the advisor sends it in her own words. The first answer ('the one from last time') does not settle it, because last time there were two things. She asks again by naming both, and the answer shows it is neither: the shake is now under braking. One draft edited after another; booked, labelled, resolved.

customer.name: Dot Kirby
customer.note: an older regular of the Bonny Oaks shop; 2012 Toyota Camry; tires balanced in March, a battery light in June

scenario.who_writes: A regular who expects Angie to know.
scenario.what_happens: Two questions before the request is clear, then a brake inspection the next morning.

facts.history: a shake at highway speed in March, cured by balancing the tires; a battery light in the mornings in June
facts.booked: the Thursday of week T-6, 09:00, at east

unclear.kind: the wrong thing named: 'that thing again' points at last time's tire balance, and it is the brakes
unclear.how: Angie asks which thing; the answer is 'the one from last time'. She names the two things of last time and asks which is back: the shaking, but now when braking downhill. That is a different job, and she says so.

T-44d.what: the Wednesday of week T-6 (DESIGN.md section 6, row 26)

timeline.text: Angie its Dot. the car is doing that thing again
Good morning, Dot! I'm sorry to hear that. Could you tell me a little more about what the car is doing?
timeline.why_a_draft: the channel is set to drafts

timeline.text:
Good morning, Dot! I'm sorry, that's no fun. Help me out, Dot: which thing is it doing again?
Angie
Thank you, Dot. I don't have your last visit in front of me. Is it a noise, a warning light, or something you feel when you drive?
timeline.why_a_draft: the channel is set to drafts

timeline.text:
We had two things, Dot, so let me chase the right one: the shake in the steering wheel on the highway, that we balanced the tires for in March, or the battery light that came on in the mornings in June. Which one is back?
Angie
but now its when I put the brakes on coming down the mountain
Thank you, Dot, that helps. A shake that comes when you brake, especially downhill, should be checked. A brake inspection is $49.95. Would you like to bring it in?
timeline.why_a_draft: the channel is set to drafts

timeline.text:
That tells me a lot, Dot. A shake when you brake coming downhill isn't the tires this time; it's most likely the front brake rotors, and if it were my car I wouldn't keep riding the mountain on them. A brake inspection is $49.95, and we'll show you what we find before anything is done. I can see you tomorrow at 9:00 or Friday at 7:30. Which is easier?
Angie
Thank you, Dot. Tomorrow at 9:00 works. See you then!
timeline.why_a_draft: the channel is set to drafts

timeline.text:
You're set, Dot: tomorrow, Thursday, at 9:00, brake inspection on the Camry, here at Bonny Oaks. Take it easy coming down today.
Angie

what she named (the thing from last time) was not what the car needed: the shake is under braking
the price named is the inspection, 49.95

why: The assistant's second draft offers three readings without knowing the history; Angie offers the two that are true.
A weaker desk would have booked a tire balance.
She still does not name a repair price: 'most likely the rotors', then the inspection.
